name: GitHub
description: Issues, pull requests, code search and reviews on the repositories you can reach.
long_description:
GitHub's own hosted MCP server. It reads and writes issues, pull requests, files, workflows and releases, using your GitHub account's permissions — it can reach exactly what you can reach, and nothing more.

There are two ways to connect. **Sign in** uses OAuth, which needs a GitHub OAuth application's client id: GitHub registers no client automatically, so either Gantry ships one or you paste your own. **Use a token** takes a fine-grained personal access token instead and works immediately.

Whichever you choose, the credential is encrypted on this machine and is never sent anywhere except to GitHub.

auth.instructions: GitHub registers no application on its own. Create one — it takes a minute, the button below fills the form in — then paste its Client ID here. Gantry keeps it, so this happens once.

auth_alternate.instructions: Create a fine-grained token with access to the repositories you want, then paste it here. Nothing else to set up.

risk.notes: Acts as you on GitHub. Merging, force-pushing and deleting are asked about every time.
